title: What is the shortest path for an ant on a cube?
description: A cube has side four centimetres, with an ant at the centre of a side face and a laddu at the centre of the top face. The board unfolds the top face beside the side face and joins the two points with a straight line. Keeko's doubt is that the ant should walk to a corner first.
teaching_notes: One idea: unfold the faces into a net, and the shortest path on the solid is a straight line on the net. Watch for students who pick a path through a corner because it looks natural.

source: A cube has side 4 cm. An ant is at the centre of a side face
video_script.why: The child finds a shortest path on a solid by unfolding the faces it crosses, because a path on the solid has the same length on the net and the shortest path on a flat sheet is a straight line.
video_script.substitution: cube of side 4 cm; ant at the centre of a side face, 2 cm below the shared edge; laddu at the centre of the top face, 2 cm beyond the shared edge, on the same straight line; path 2 + 2 = 4 cm.
video_script.anchor: the cube of the book with the ant and the laddu, the top face unfolded above the side face
video_script.wrong_answer: the ant should walk to a corner first
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sends the ant to a corner first and then across to the laddu; on the flat net this route bends at the corner and is about 5.7 cm, longer than the 4 cm straight line, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The shortest path is four centimetres, a straight line up the middle of the side face

final_answer.value: 4 cm, straight up the middle of the side face and across to the centre of the top
final_answer.spoken: four centimetres, straight up the middle of the side face and across to the centre of the top

hold_back: 4 cm, straight up the middle of the side face and across to the centre of the top
maths_rules: a path on the cube and the matching path on the net have the same length
on a flat sheet the shortest path between two points is the straight line
unfold the top face so it lies flat above the side face; both faces are 4 cm by 4 cm
the ant is at the centre of the side face: 2 cm below the shared edge; the laddu is at the centre of the top face: 2 cm beyond the shared edge, on the same vertical line
wrong idea: via the corner, 2 root 2 + 2 root 2 = 4 root 2, about 5.66 cm, which is longer than 4 cm
video_script.design: One idea: unfold, then draw a straight line. The top face swings down beside the side face on the stage; the straight line is drawn in the accent colour and the corner route in the warning colour.
